title: Medicine and the body
summary: Instruments, conditions and the people who treat them.

questions.clue: A doctor uses this instrument to listen to your heart and your lungs.
questions.note: From the Greek for chest and examine. It is the object hanging round the neck in every photograph of a doctor.

questions.clue: This is a doctor who is trained to perform operations.
questions.note: A physician treats illness with medicine; a surgeon operates. In British hospitals a senior surgeon is called Mister rather than Doctor.

questions.clue: This is the shop where you hand in a prescription and collect your medicine.
questions.note: Chemist is the usual British word and drugstore the American one, so all three are accepted.

questions.clue: This is a strip of soft cloth wrapped around a wound to protect it while it heals.
questions.note: A dressing is the pad placed directly on the wound and a bandage holds it there, but the words are used interchangeably in ordinary speech.

questions.clue: This is an injection that teaches your body to resist a disease before you ever catch it.
questions.note: The vaccine is the substance and the vaccination is the act of giving it. Jab is informal British English for the same thing.

questions.clue: This is a sign in your body that suggests you are ill, such as a headache or a rash.
questions.note: A symptom is what the patient notices. What the doctor observes and measures is called a sign.

questions.clue: This is the complete framework of bones that supports your body.
questions.note: An adult human skeleton has two hundred and six bones. A baby is born with about three hundred, and many of them fuse together.

questions.clue: This is a harmful reaction your body has to something that is usually harmless, like pollen or nuts.
questions.note: The immune system treats a safe substance as a threat. The substance itself is called an allergen.

questions.clue: This is the drug given before an operation so that the patient feels no pain.
questions.note: British English keeps the a before the e; American English drops it. Both spellings are accepted here.

questions.clue: This is the medical word for the regular beating of your heart, counted in beats per minute.
questions.note: Strictly the pulse is the wave you can feel in an artery, produced by each heartbeat, but either word answers the clue.
